standard_prerequisites.name: Properties of the henselization of a local ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, the lemmas that the henselization of a reduced ring is reduced, that it preserves dimension and Noetherianness, and that the local ring maps faithfully flatly into its henselization
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the reducedness, dimension and Noetherianness of the henselian local ring and the injectivity of the map on total rings of fractions.

core_obligations: Reduce to an elementary etale neighbourhood (proof lines 793-806): take an elementary etale neighbourhood (U, u) of (X, xi); since U is locally Noetherian and reduced, the local ring at u is a one dimensional reduced Noetherian ring, and after shrinking U one may assume every irreducible component passes through u and that U is affine and Noetherian.

Produce the map from the function field (proof lines 806-814): since the map U -> X is open and X is irreducible it is dominant, which gives a ring map from the function field of X to that of U by composing rational maps; the source is a field so this map is injective, and by the choice of U the function field of U is the total quotient ring of the local ring at u.

Pass to the henselization (proof lines 816-826): the henselian local ring is the henselization of that local ring, hence reduced, one dimensional and Noetherian by the general properties of henselization; since the local ring maps faithfully flatly into its henselization, nonzerodivisors are preserved, so the identification of the total quotient rings gives the required canonical injective map.
proof_roadmap: Replace the space by an elementary etale neighbourhood in which the local ring has the expected properties.
Compose rational maps to get an injective map of function fields and identify the target with a total quotient ring.
Use the properties of henselization and its faithful flatness to reach the henselian local ring.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for the generic point of a prime divisor on a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space the henselian local ring is reduced, one dimensional and Noetherian, and that the function field maps canonically and injectively into its total ring of fractions (statement lines 779-790). The proof (proof lines 792-835) passes to an elementary etale neighbourhood, composes rational maps to get an injective map of function fields, identifies the target with a total quotient ring, and transfers the statement to the henselization using its general properties and faithful flatness. H2: a three-step reduction with three inputs, written out in full.
